Question_text: AHG is an established business as it has been operating for a long time. It sells garden products including plants and flowers. AHG uses competitive pricing. The business has 4 managers and 30 other employees. All AHG's managers use delegation. The Finance Manager is analysing AHG's statement of financial position as she is interested in its liquidity. An extract is shown in Table 1.1. Table 1.1 Extract from AHG's statement of financial position at 30 March 2022 ($000) Non-current assets 800 Current assets 660 Current liabilities 600
image: Table 1.1 titled 'Extract from AHG's statement of financial position at 30 March 2022 ($000)' with three rows: 'Non-current assets' with value 800, 'Current assets' with value 660, and 'Current liabilities' with value 600. All values are in $000.
Sub_topic: Importance of delegation, trust vs control
Pricing methods: cost plus, competitive, penetration, skimming, promotional

Parts.part_text: Define 'current liabilities'.
Identify two examples of non-current assets.
Outline two possible reasons why liquidity is important to AHG.
Explain two advantages to AHG of its managers using delegation.
Do you think competitive pricing is the best method for an established business to use? Justify your answer.

Question_text: RWB manufactures buses. 1200 people work in its factory. All employees receive off-the-job training. RWB uses financial rewards to motivate its employees. Last year RWB made a $1.7 million loss. The Managing Director said: 'There are many external influences affecting our business, including changes in the level of unemployment and new legal controls over business activities which affect the environment.'
Sub_topic: Benefits, limitations: induction, on-the-job, off-the-job training
Reasons people work, meaning of motivation
Financial rewards: wage, salary, bonus, commission, profit sharing
Stages of business cycle: growth, boom, recession, slump

Parts.part_text: Define 'off-the-job training'.
Identify two reasons (other than financial) why people work.
Outline two methods of financial rewards RWB might use to motivate its employees.
Explain two ways RWB might be affected by new legal controls over business activities which affect the environment.
Do you think a reduction in the level of unemployment always benefits businesses? Justify your answer.

Question_text: CHW manufactures electrical products including cameras. The business is developing new products. The Managing Director knows that the stage of the product life cycle can influence CHW's marketing decisions about promotion. He is analysing data for one of its products. An extract is shown in Table 3.1. The business would also like to introduce flow production into the factory. Table 3.1 Extract from CHW's data for one type of camera (2021) Selling price per unit ($) 120 Variable cost per unit ($) 40 Fixed costs ($) 200 000 Margin of safety (units) 500
image: Table 3.1 titled 'Extract from CHW's data for one type of camera (2021)' with rows: 'Selling price per unit ($)' with value 120, 'Variable cost per unit ($)' with value 40, 'Fixed costs ($)' with value 200 000, and 'Margin of safety (units)' with value 500.
Sub_topic: Define, calculate, interpret margin of safety
Product life cycle: stages, extension strategies
Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production

Parts.part_text: Identify one benefit and one cost to a business of developing new products.
Calculate the break-even level of output for 2021. Show your working.
Outline two ways CHW could increase its margin of safety.
Explain two ways in which the stage of the product life cycle might affect CHW's marketing decisions about promotion.
Do you think flow production is the best method of production for a manufacturing business to use? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Tom wants to leave his job to become an entrepreneur. He and his sister plan to start a window cleaning business. Tom has been told that new businesses are at a greater risk of failure than established businesses. Tom has to decide whether a partnership is a suitable form of business organisation for the new business. He has calculated the business will need $700 as start-up capital. Tom knows that every decision he makes will have an opportunity cost.
Sub_topic: Concepts of needs, wants, scarcity, opportunity cost
Causes of failure: management skills, environment changes, liquidity
Reasons for finance: start-up, expansion, working capital
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures

Parts.part_text: Define 'entrepreneur'.
Define 'opportunity cost'.
Identify four reasons why a new business might be at greater risk of failure than an established business.
Explain two suitable sources of start-up capital Tom's business might use.
Do you think a partnership is the best form of business organisation for a new business? Justify your answer.
